timeline.change: Revealed 9 April on the TNGA-F (GA-F) frame shared with the Tacoma; production delayed to December by parts shortages
Launch: 2.4 turbo i-Force (278 hp) or i-Force Max hybrid (326 hp), eight-speed auto, nine trims including new Trailhunter and Platinum; towing up to 6,000 lb
No major changes reported by Car and Driver

identify.intro: Nine trims share a body, so drivetrain and off-road hardware are what separate a $44k truck from a $70k one.

items.head: Model codes
items.body: TZNA50/55 for the gas 2.4 turbo i-Force; TZNH55 for the i-Force Max hybrid (4WD only).

items.head: Hybrid or not
items.body: i-Force Max is standard on Platinum, TRD Pro and Trailhunter, and optional on TRD Off-Road, TRD Off-Road Premium and Limited. The hybrid battery sits under the load floor, so hybrids have no third-row option (Car and Driver).

items.head: Trailhunter
items.body: Old Man Emu 2.5 in forged shocks with rear remote reservoirs, ARB-designed roof rack, high-mounted intake, steel skids, about 2 in more front and 1.5 in more rear clearance, heritage grille with bronze TOYOTA letters, and a 20 in LED light bar.

items.head: 4WD system
items.body: Part-time 4WD with low range on most trims; full-time 4WD with a locking centre diff on Platinum and some Limiteds.

values.intro: New-car pricing. The hybrid-only TRD Pro and Trailhunter sit at the top, and there's no meaningful used market yet.
values.note: MSRP ranges from Car and Driver's 2026 4Runner and 4Runner Hybrid pages, excluding destination and options.
